issues.description: The problem statement is inconsistent about whether acceptSupplyDelivery should be static. In the UML excerpt (problem_statement.md lines 25-34) acceptSupplyDelivery is shown as a regular public instance method (+acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int): void) with no static qualifier, while the textual specification later (problem_statement.md lines 77-80) explicitly requires acceptSupplyDelivery to be static because it manages the shared stock. The solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery as static (SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery), which matches the textual requirement but conflicts with the UML depiction. This inconsistency can confuse students about the intended signature and whether they should declare the method static.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: either update the UML snippet to show acceptSupplyDelivery as static (e.g., indicate <<static>> or similar notation) or remove the textual requirement that it be static. Preferably, clarify in the specification that acceptSupplyDelivery is static (shared stock) and update the UML to match so students implement the static method as in the solution.
